facts.raw_span: Visual acuity: 20/25 to 20/30 in both eyes (OU)
Few yellow spots present, no pigmentary degeneration
Indistinct grayish circle beyond the arcades
Large, slow scotopic and photopic responses
Complete loss of photoreceptors, ellipsoid zone, and retinal pigment epithelium in superotemporal region
Visual acuity: 20/25 to 20/30 in both eyes (OU)
Few yellow spots present, no pigmentary degeneration
Indistinct grayish circle beyond the arcades
Large, slow scotopic and photopic responses
Complete loss of photoreceptors, ellipsoid zone, and retinal pigment epithelium in superotemporal region

concepts.why: The patient's night blindness since childhood, flat rod electroretinogram, and complete loss of photoreceptors in the superotemporal region are consistent with Retinitis pigmentosa.
The patient's night blindness, superotemporal zones showing hypofluorescence, and complete loss of photoreceptors in the superotemporal region are consistent with Choroideremia.
The patient's night blindness, inferonasal scotoma, and complete loss of photoreceptors in the superotemporal region are consistent with Gyrate atrophy.
The patient's night blindness since childhood, normal color vision, and clear central macula are consistent with Congenital stationary night blindness.
The patient's night blindness since childhood, flat rod electroretinogram, and complete loss of photoreceptors in the superotemporal region are consistent with Leber congenital amaurosis.

rationales.F01: Night blindness since childhood is a key symptom of retinal disorders
rationales.F07: Inferonasal scotoma is a characteristic visual field defect in certain retinal disorders
rationales.F09: Flat rod electroretinogram is a diagnostic feature of retinitis pigmentosa and congenital stationary night blindness
rationales.F11: Complete loss of photoreceptors, ellipsoid zone, and retinal pigment epithelium in the superotemporal region is a characteristic feature of choroideremia and retinitis pigmentosa

frontier_selector.rationale: Retinitis pigmentosa best explains the combination of night blindness since childhood, flat rod electroretinogram, and specific structural changes like complete loss of photoreceptors and retinal pigment epithelium in the superotemporal region, without strong contradictions.
